To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the membership choice is sensible to the availability of parking, the price of parking, the distance of parking and the location of the activities in relation to parking and that these supply characteristics impact the membership choice in different way for round trip and free-floating carsharing.

1) the membership of round trip carsharing is more sensible to the availability of parking spaces and the distance from the center, 2) free floating carsharing membership is more sensible to parking prices and to the availability of the car owned by the member.
the membership choice is sensible to supply characteristics, such as parking price and availability, and to the user's travel chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the supply characteristics that influence membership choice in roundtrip and free floating car sharing services.
the analysis of the impact that the supply characteristics have on membership choice and the identification of two typical profiles of users.
the impact of supply characteristics on membership choice and it is a step toward the development of a model that could be used to forecast demand for carsharing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the membership choice is driven by the type of trip chain and the parking availability.
a round trip member is more likely to be a carless person while the free floating member is a car owner.
the membership choice is driven by the type of trip scheme the user is willing to use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
round trip membership choice is more influenced by parking supply attributes, while free floating membership choice is more affected by trip chain and distance to the city center attributes.
the membership choice is influenced by the supply attributes and the user characteristics, which are not independent from the supply attributes.
the supply characteristics of the round trip carsharing system are more suitable for a member that is more willing to have a car available and is more likely to have a trip chain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the carsharing system to use is not only influenced by the user characteristics, but is also influenced by the characteristics of the supply.
supply characteristics are not equally important for the two carsharing services, and that they are more relevant for the free floating one.
the membership choice is influenced by different factors and that the supply characteristics have to be tailored to each specific service.
